rationale:
Use ANALYTICS.MARTS.DIM_CUSTOMER_CONTACTABLE. It is the only candidate where the filter that makes an outbound send lawful has already been applied: consent granted, not unsubscribed, not subject to a deletion request. It carries a Governance.ConsentFiltered glossary term, a passing SQL assertion that no row has a null consent timestamp, a technical owner in analytics and a business owner in legal.privacy, and it was refreshed four hours ago.

The count is the tell. This table holds 5.1 million rows against 8.0 million in the raw customer table. That 2.9 million row gap is not staleness - it is the people who never consented, unsubscribed, or asked to be forgotten. Any candidate with a higher row count is higher precisely because it has not applied the filter, so on this question a bigger number is the signal that you have the wrong table.

traps.why: An unowned, undocumented ad-hoc export of 7.9 million email addresses, untouched since November 2025. It predates nine months of unsubscribes and deletion requests, so sending to it mails people who have since opted out or exercised erasure rights. It has no owner to ask and no consent column to filter on.

The live application table - fresh, complete, and tagged PII with column-level PII.Email and PII.Name terms. It has no consent or unsubscribe column at all, so there is no correct way to filter it for marketing use. Its completeness is the hazard: all 8.0 million rows include the 2.9 million people who must not be contacted.
